title: MedlinePlus says newborns often lose about a tenth of birth weight, then gain
summary: MedlinePlus says a newborn normally loses about 10 to 12 percent of birth weight, and that gain is under way by about 2 weeks.
body: The MedlinePlus growth page says that soon after birth an infant normally loses about 10 to 12 percent of birth weight. It says that by about age 2 weeks the infant starts to gain weight and grow quickly. Normally, on that page, describes the early loss. The two-week mark is when the page says gain begins. This is one encyclopedia's account of the usual pattern. It is not a target for one newborn, and a clinician reads the baby's own record.

sources.title: Normal growth and development
sources.author: MedlinePlus
sources.note: Supports the early loss of about 10 to 12 percent of birth weight and the start of gain by about 2 weeks.
